channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Colby Parkinson caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: Parkinson was barely involved today, though he nearly scored a touchdown on the Rams’ sixth drive. He successfully high-pointed a red zone pass, but tumbled out of bounds at the one-yard line, tangled up with a Cardinals defender. Parkinson will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Tyler Higbee caught 3-of-4 targets for 17 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: Higbee earned an end zone target on the Rams’ opening drive, but Matthew Stafford overthrew him, resulting in an incompletion. The two did manage to link up for a score on the Rams’ fourth drive, though. Rams coach Sean McVay dialed up a play where Higbee motioned from in-line to out wide on the left side. He ran right past his coverage defender, and Stafford hit him streaking toward the back of the end zone for a five-yard touchdown. Higbee will likely be a low-end TE1 against the Packers, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Davis Allen caught 1-of-1 targets in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: Allen played a small role, but made a big impact today, scoring from 19 yards out on a nice catch-and-run on the Rams’ seventh drive. Allen lined up in-line on the right side before slipping across the field mid-play, seemingly without any Cardinals defenders noticing. He easily hauled in the pass and turned upfield for the score. Allen will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Packers, post-bye, in Week 12.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Xavier Smith caught 2-of-2 targets for 40 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: Smith could have scored a 72-yard touchdown on the Rams’ third drive, but he was brought down by a shoestring tackle while trying to turn upfield. He made up for it with a 22-yard screen pass touchdown on the Rams’ fifth drive, in which he weaved through the middle of the field before cutting north into the end zone. The Rams go on bye next week, before facing the Packers in Week 12. He does not qualify as a much-stash player at this time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Konata Mumpfield caught 3-of-4 targets for 81 yards in the Rams’ Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: Mumpfield had a decent game today, producing catches of 10, 27 and 45 yards, notably adding decent yardage post-catch on his two longest receptions. He was also targeted on Matthew Stafford’s interception, but it was simply an off-target throw. Mumpfield generated his longest gain with a slick hitch-and-go, leaving his defender in the dust on the false step. The Rams go on bye in Week 11 and face the Packers in Week 12. Davante Adams (hamstring) is targeting a Week 13 return. Mumpfield should be FLEX-viable in Week 12, though he will likely become quite volatile when Adams returns.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: George Pickens caught 11-of-18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
item.description: In his first game since owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys needed to focus more on getting the ball to Pickens, the 25-year-old receiver saw passes funneled to him early and often. Pickens was targeted six times on the Cowboys’ first two drives and capped the second drive with a 35-yard touchdown to give the Cowboys their first touchdown of the day. Pickens would find the end zone two more times in this one, with his second score coming on a 39-yard play on a long catch-and-run. His last score would come on a five-yard pass from Dak Prescott as the Cowboys aimed to keep pace with the Niners late in the fourth quarter, but it ultimately proved to not be enough in the end. Despite his struggles at various points this season, Pickens was far from an underutilized receiver, as he entered the day averaging a solid 7.8 targets per game. It goes without saying that we shouldn’t expect this kind of performance every week from Pickens, but he will be on the fantasy radar next week as a mid-to-high-end WR2.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Christian McCaffrey rushed 13 times for 62 yards and one touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 10 win over the Cowboys, adding four receptions for 161 yards and two touchdowns.
Dak Prescott completed 30-of-51 passes for 343 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 46-40, Week 10 loss to the 49ers.
Brock Purdy completed 22-of-28 passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns in the 49ers’ 46-40, Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
item.description: Facing a porous Cowboys defense, Purdy and the Niners delivered just about everything fantasy managers could have hoped for in this one. Despite taking five sacks on the day, Purdy was nearly perfect, throwing just six incompletions while coming up with multiple big plays. Purdy’s first touchdown pass came on an 11-yard bubble screen to Deebo Samuel, with his other two coming on long catch-and-runs by Christian McCaffrey. In the second quarter, Purdy tossed a 14-yard pass to McCaffrey, which CMC immediately turned upfield for a 74-yard score, and in the fourth quarter, another six-yard pass to CMC in the face of a blitz resulted in a 66-yard score after the Cowboys left Von Miller in coverage against McCaffrey. Purdy’s three touchdowns resulted in 151 passing yards, but came on passes that combined for just 20 air yards. That’s the benefit of playing with elite playmakers like CMC. Purdy and the Niners will get a true test in Week 11 when they take on the Vikings in Mexico City. We cautiously project Purdy as a QB1 despite the tough matchup on paper.-Zachary Krueger

item.title: Matthew Stafford completed 18-of-26 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Rams’ 34-6, Week 10 win over the Cardinals.
item.description: The Rams lost two centers to injury today, but Stafford navigated the resulting offensive line shuffling without issue, completing passes to nine different pass catchers. Stafford probably should have had a fourth touchdown added to his box score, but he overthrew Tyler Higbee and CJ Daniels in the end zone on the opening drive, which ultimately resulted in a field goal. A touchdown pass thrown to Kyren Williams was called back due to a false start on the Rams’ fourth drive, but Stafford linked up with Higbee for a score a couple of plays later. A similar sequence occurred in which Stafford threw a touchdown pass to Xavier Smith on the following drive, after Tutu Atwell failed to secure what should have been a 32-yard touchdown. Stafford’s second-drive interception was on him. He threw an off-target pass to Konatha Mumpfield, which a Cardinals defender easily caught. All in all, Stafford dealt with the Rams’ offensive personnel issues well. He will be a low-end QB1 against the Packers in Week 12, following the Rams’ Week 11 bye.-Nic Bodiford
